spl:
index=alerts sourcetype="pagerduty:incident"
| eval created_epoch=coalesce(created_at_epoch, strptime(created_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
| eval ack_epoch=coalesce(first_acknowledgement_at_epoch, strptime(first_acknowledgement_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
| eval ack_delay_sec=ack_epoch-created_epoch
| eval step_timeout=coalesce(escalation_policy_step_timeout_sec, 600)
| eval missed_step=if(isnull(ack_epoch) OR ack_delay_sec > step_timeout,1,0)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as inc, sum(missed_step) as missed by _time, escalation_policy, service_name
| eval timeout_rate=round(100*missed/nullif(inc,0),2)
| where timeout_rate > 15 AND inc >= 5
| sort -timeout_rate

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure: PagerDuty REST API poller or Event Orchestration webhook normalizer.
• Data: `index=alerts` `sourcetype=pagerduty:incident` with `escalation_policy`, `escalation_levels`, `first_acknowledgement_at`, `created_at`.
• For directory layout and inputs, see docs/implementation-guide.md.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Map `step_timeout` from exported escalation policy JSON if not on each incident. Treat `missed` carefully for low-urgency incidents. Pair with schedule coverage UCs for root cause.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following search (then save as report or alert; tune time range and threshold):

```spl
index=alerts sourcetype="pagerduty:incident"
| eval created_epoch=coalesce(created_at_epoch, strptime(created_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
| eval ack_epoch=coalesce(first_acknowledgement_at_epoch, strptime(first_acknowledgement_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
| eval ack_delay_sec=ack_epoch-created_epoch
| eval step_timeout=coalesce(escalation_policy_step_timeout_sec, 600)
| eval missed_step=if(isnull(ack_epoch) OR ack_delay_sec > step_timeout,1,0)
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as inc, sum(missed_step) as missed by _time, escalation_policy, service_name
| eval timeout_rate=round(100*missed/nullif(inc,0),2)
| where timeout_rate > 15 AND inc >= 5
| sort -timeout_rate
```

Understanding this search
Escalation policies encode contractual response times; when acknowledgements consistently arrive after configured step timeouts, teams burn trust in paging and auto-escalations become noise. Measuring timeout_rate per policy surfaces rotation and training gaps.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with the PagerDuty incident timeline and service view for the same window. Reconcile a few incident numbers, state changes, and acknowledgement times. If anything disagrees, check export lag, time zone, and which API fields we map.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add to a dashboard, wire alert actions, and document ownership. Suggested view: Line chart (timeout_rate by policy), stacked bar (missed vs met), table of worst services.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (PagerDuty REST API poller or Event Orchestration webhook normalizer — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=pagerduty:incident into alerts. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, created_at, escalation_policy, first_acknowledgement_at`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We measure how often incidents are not acknowledged within the time your playbook allows. If that happens a lot, the escalation ladder is not matching real life.
